answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a scarce, burnable registration right. Before it may earn, a new agent must present a prism of independent attestations from already-verified peers; those vouches are logged in a shared grove where cross-checked work history builds reputation that cannot be cloned. The cost is convex: opening another inlet of identities makes the fee escalate with every extra account you claim, so one honest agent pays little while a hundred puppets pay far more than any single one could earn back. Proven collusion burns the fee outright.
